reasons: No tests are visible in the packet.
The time limit and size limits are fixed numbers in the code.
Some extension handling is shared between two lists, which can drift apart.

terms.meaning: The recorded outcome for an item, such as pending, failed or processed.
A fingerprint of a file's bytes, used to find identical copies.
A separate file that stores extra information about another file.

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Constants and supported file types
sections.what: Sets the extraction version, the size limits for the index and each document, and the list of file types the extractor supports, including PDF, images, Office files and DXF.
sections.why: Keeping the supported list in one place decides which files are read and which are skipped.
sections.watch_out: Adding a file type here without a matching reader will leave it unprocessed.

sections.name: bounded_json
sections.title: Reading a size-checked JSON file
sections.what: Reads a JSON file after checking its size, and returns it as a dictionary.
sections.why: The size check stops a huge file from being loaded into memory.
sections.watch_out: Invalid text or invalid JSON is not caught here, so the caller receives the raw error.

sections.name: publish
sections.title: Publishing a JSON file safely
sections.what: Writes JSON to a temporary file and then replaces the target. Retries a few times if Windows is holding the file, and never deletes the old report or changes file permissions.
sections.why: Likely reason: Windows often locks files briefly, and writing to a temporary file avoids leaving a half-written report.
sections.watch_out: After eight failed attempts the error is raised, so the caller must handle a report that could not be saved.

sections.name: auxiliary
sections.title: Identifying helper files to skip
sections.what: Recognises Windows thumbnail database files and Office lock files, which are not real content.
sections.why: Skipping them stops noise from being extracted as documents.

sections.name: _retain_pdf_diagnostics
sections.title: Attaching parser diagnostics
sections.what: Adds the parser's receipt to a document record under a parser diagnostics field.
sections.why: Reason not stated in the code beyond the field name. It appears to keep parser details with the document.

sections.name: summary
sections.title: Shortening a record for summaries
sections.what: Returns a copy of a document record without its bulky content, keeping only summary fields and each unit's kind, name, part, page, disposition and limitations.
sections.why: Lets the app show a document list without carrying all the extracted text.
sections.watch_out: Only the listed unit fields are kept, so any new field must be added to the list to appear in summaries.

sections.name: extract_package_documents (part 1)
sections.title: Starting document extraction
sections.what: Requires a complete inventory, creates a new output folder, groups entries by content hash and sets up the receipt. Defines a checkpoint that stops for cancellation or after 900 seconds, then begins the loop over each unique file with progress reporting.
sections.why: Grouping by hash means each unique file is processed once, however many paths point to it.
sections.watch_out: The 900 second limit is hard-coded, so large packages can hit it and fail.

sections.name: extract_package_documents (part 2)
sections.title: Processing each unique document
sections.what: For each unique file, checks that its alias file types agree. It then either marks the file as not read (Office lock or thumbnail files, schedule files waiting for a parser, unsupported types) or copies it into the output and reads its content. A failure is recorded on that document and does not stop the whole run unless the run is cancelled.
sections.why: Likely reason: one unreadable file should not stop a whole package from being processed, so each file's outcome is recorded separately.
sections.watch_out: A failure is recorded rather than raised, so a document can look handled when its content was never read. Always check the disposition and error fields.

sections.name: extract_package_documents (part 3)
sections.title: Recording results and failed PDF pages
sections.what: Sets each document's final status. A PDF needs visual review if any page has no text, needs review, or has limitations. A PDF is marked failed if a page warning says it could not be read or was cut short. Drawings and other Office files get their own statuses. The per-document record is then saved, and if it is too large, a short failed summary is saved instead.
sections.why: Likely reason: a record that is too large would otherwise break the save, so a smaller failed summary is written instead.
sections.watch_out: Failed PDF pages are found by matching words in warning messages, so a change in the PDF library's wording could hide a real failure.

sections.name: extract_package_documents (part 4)
sections.title: Writing the run receipt and totals
sections.what: Stores each document's summary in the index, writes the overall receipt, and sets the complete flag only after every step finishes. A final block always runs, even after an error. It counts dispositions, lists failed documents, and sets whether all supported content was processed.
sections.why: Likely reason: the final block writes the totals even after an error, so a failed run still leaves a readable record.
sections.watch_out: The receipt is saved even after an error, so check the complete flag and error field rather than whether the file exists. A complete run does not prove that every document was understood.

summary: Extracts text and data from each unique document in a package, stores one result per unique file, and records a disposition for every reference.
purpose: Gives the rest of the app a complete, checkable record of what was read from a package, including what was skipped and why.
why: Likely reason: processing each unique file once saves time, and a receipt for every reference keeps the process accountable.
how: Requires a completed inventory. Groups the entries by content hash, then for each unique file picks a candidate name and runs the matching reader. Writes results to a sources folder, applies a 15 minute time limit and supports cancellation.
inputs: An inventory file, an empty output folder, a cancel check and a progress callback.
outputs: A receipt with one document record per unique file, the coverage counts and the processing status, written into the output folder.
risks: The 15 minute time limit is fixed, so very large packages can fail. The output folder must not already exist.
debug: Check that the inventory is complete. Read the receipt's core processing failures and each document's disposition. A failed document shows its reason in its record.
